title: A two-gene prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《A two-gene prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Aims · abstract-1-1】This study aimed to develop accurate prognostic assessment tools for patients with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) using Summary-data-based Mendelian Randomization Analysis and statistical learning-based prognostic modeling methods.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Extensive population-based studies have repeatedly demonstrated that lung cancer ranks among the most prevalent malignancies globally and represents the primary contributor to cancer-associated deaths [1]. Recent data from 2020 revealed that diagnostic centers identified upwards of 220,000 individuals with this condition, while mortality statistics indicated over 180,000 fatalities attributed to pulmonary malignancies [2]. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), constituting the majority subtype, represents roughly 85% of all lung cancer cases [3]. Within this category, lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) accounts for approximately 65% of these diagnoses [3]. Current therapeutic approaches for this condition include molecularly targeted agents and immune-based therapies, reflecting a comprehensive, multimodal treatment paradigm [4]. Despite substantial improvements in diagnostic techniques and therapeutic modalities that have progressively increased patient survival, the disease continues to exhibit poor clinical outcomes [5]. In addition, due to its molecular diversity and frequent late-stage diagnosis, it poses significant clinical challenges. Therefore, it is critical to identify additional biomarkers to facilitate early detection and prognostic evaluation in LUAD. Such advancements could enhance risk classification and improve patient survival. Computational approaches applied to omics datasets have shown notable promise in identifying disease biomarkers. However, traditional analyses of gene expression-disease relationships are often confounded by external influences, such as environmental factors and lifestyle, as well as issues of reverse causation [6]. Pathological changes may alter gene expression profiles rather than result from them, complicating efforts to establish genuine genetic associations. Furthermore, observational studies face challenges in disentangling the complex interactions among genetic predisposition, environmental exposures, and disease progression [7]. In addition, previous studies have developed radiomics-based [8] and bioinformatics-based [9] prognostic models for lung cancer, providing complementary perspectives to the present work.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《A two-gene prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We conducted SMR analysis to explore genetic associations between genes and LUAD, and analyzed differentially expressed genes (DEGs). The shared genes were subjected to the univariate Cox regression analysis and survival analysis to determine prognosis-related genes to construct a prognostic model with the multivariate Cox regression analysis. Individual gene contributions to the model were clarified through SHAP analysis, and predictive performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic curve, the C-index, and calibration plots.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《A two-gene prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】59 shared genes were identified between the SMR and DEGs analyses. The univariate Cox regression analysis and survival analysis identified two prognosis-related genes (PKP2 and SLC7A11), which were used to develop a prognostic model. The Kaplan-Meier plot and univariate and multivariate Cox regression models illustrated that patients in the high-risk group had a poorer clinical outcome. The low-risk group showed enrichment of several immune-related pathways and showed higher infiltration levels of 15 immune cell types.

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】A two-gene prognostic model was developed to predict outcomes in patients with LUAD, which was also highly associated with immune status.

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《A two-gene prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Data availability statement · S0008-p1】LUAD eQTL data were obtained from the FinnGen database (Consortium, 2013; Consortium, 2020; https://www.finngen.fi/en), which contains 27,046 genes on autosomal chromosomes. We gathered four gene expression profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA; https://www.cancer.gov) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov) databases: TCGA-LUAD, GSE68465 (GEO cohort 1), GSE31210 (GEO cohort 2), and GSE41271 (GEO cohort 3). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data (GSE123902) were also obtained from the GEO database.
